messages.subject: would basically need a global variable in the model block - any tricks around this?
parts:
Hi Stan users,

I am fairly new to Stan but already a big fan (very powerful for the first models I have tested!).

Now I encountered an interesting problem which I think others must have before too (though skimming through the list I could not find an answer yet):

Basically I have a latent variable, which requires both transformation and sampling (it's goodwill carried forward and requires another parameter to estimate the weight from the previous goodwill vs. the new observation).

For the first model I ran (which converged fine), I simply defined this latent variable in the model block. Unfortunately, this makes it a local variable that gets lost afterwards.

The issue here is that I would need this variable to include in my log-likelihood calculation (done in the generated quantities block - also to use the loo-package later on). But because it was a local variable (defined in model block), I lost it . 

However, I seem not to be able to put the latent-variable transformation in the "transformed parameter block" (which defines global variables) as I am not allowed to do any sampling outside of the model block.

Simply defining/ creating the latent variable in the "transformed parameter block" and adding the calculation in the model block later does not work either (error msg: "wrong side of equation").

What would be the solution to this problem? And why are there no global variables possible in the model block (or are there)?

Thanks
John

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] would basically need a global variable in the model block - any tricks around this?
parts:
Yes, this comes up regularly, but Google groups are impossible
to search (no page rank info).

What you need to do is either

1. Declare *and* define the variable in transformed variables,
but make all the density contributions (sampling statements
or increment_log_prob) in the model block; the variables will
be visible in both the model block and generated quantities block.

2. write a function that provides the value and recompute it
in the generated quantities block. This isn't as expensive
as it sounds because we don't need to compute derivatives.

- Bob
